_comment_overview: Claude Code settings for Yale YCRC HPC clusters (targeted at Bouchet).
Philosophy: SECURITY FIRST. Prompt for confirmation on anything destructive.
These settings favor safety over speed — you will be asked before writes,
DEPENDENCY MANAGEMENT: Always prefer conda/mamba for installing packages.
Use pip only when a package is not available via conda-forge. When creating
For reproducibility, export: conda env export > environment.yml
LOGIN NODE POLICY: Lightweight orchestration (e.g. snakemake dispatching
jobs to SLURM, git, file inspection, conda env management) is fine on login
nodes. Heavy computation (actual data processing, model training, large I/O)
MUST be submitted as SLURM jobs.
_comment_cluster_info: Bouchet is the successor to Grace and McCleary. Grace is retired and
McCleary is now YCGA-only. Note the account model differs from the old
clusters: your primary group is your NetID and PI groups are pi_<netid>.
=== Storage (DO NOT run heavy I/O on login nodes) ===
All storage is on the Roberts all-flash NFS filesystem under /nfs/roberts.
There is NO GPFS and NO /vast/palmer on Bouchet.
No sensitive or regulated data on Bouchet — use the Hopper cluster.
day:          up to 24h, general purpose (DEFAULT) — 1000 CPUs/user
devel:        up to 6h interactive/test (default for salloc) — 4 CPUs, 2 jobs
bigmem:       up to 24h on 4 TiB nodes — 128 CPUs/user
mpi:          up to 2 days, tightly-coupled multi-node — 48 nodes/user
gpu:          up to 2 days — rtx_5000_ada (32GB), a40 (48GB), l40s (48GB)
gpu_devel:    up to 6h GPU testing — 2 GPUs, 1 job
scavenge:     up to 24h, preemptible, uses idle private nodes
scavenge_gpu: up to 24h, preemptible GPU nodes
Request GPUs by type: --gpus=h200:1  (none are allocated by default)
Default walltime is 1 hour on ALL partitions.
YCRC enforces job submission rate limits — use job arrays or dsq.
Interactive OOD apps: max 4 simultaneous instances.
Use 'module reset', NOT 'module purge'. module reset restores the sticky
StdEnv module that sets CONDA_ENVS_PATH, SLURM_HINT and the /apps/bin PATH
entry; module purge strips it and leaves a broken environment.
- NEVER run heavy computation on login nodes (login1.bouchet, etc.)
- Lightweight orchestration IS OK on login nodes: snakemake dispatching,
git operations, conda env management, file inspection, editing scripts
- Request only the resources your job actually needs
- Use 'module reset' + 'module load' for software, not manual PATH installs
- Scratch files older than 30 days are AUTOMATICALLY DELETED on Bouchet
- Do NOT artificially extend scratch file expiration
- Use job arrays or Dead Simple Queue for many similar jobs:
- No sensitive or regulated data on any cluster except Hopper
- YCRC does not formally support AI coding agents on the clusters:
Each rule becomes an independent SLURM job; Snakemake handles dependency
ordering and job submission automatically. The snakemake process itself
runs on the login node as a lightweight orchestrator — this is acceptable.
Install (once):    conda create -n snakemake -c conda-forge -c bioconda snakemake snakemake-executor-plugin-slurm

Then run with profile: snakemake --profile slurm

Use tmux when running snakemake on login nodes to survive disconnects:
(Ctrl-b d to detach, tmux attach -t pipeline to reconnect)
Prefer conda/mamba over pip wherever possible.
Always use conda-forge as the primary channel.
Create env:        conda create -n myenv -c conda-forge python=3.11 <pkgs>
From file:         conda env create -f environment.yml
Export env:        conda env export > environment.yml
Pip fallback:      pip install <pkg>   (only if not in conda-forge)
Remove env:        conda env remove -n myenv
Store envs in your project directory or home, NOT in scratch (purged at 30 days).

_comment_defaultMode: Starts in plan mode: Claude can read and analyze but cannot modify or execute.
Switch to acceptEdits mode with shift+tab when you're ready for Claude to act.
This prevents accidental writes to shared filesystems or unintended job submissions.
_comment_edits: Edit/Write are intentionally NOT listed here. Permission rules are
evaluated deny -> ask -> allow BEFORE the permission mode is consulted,
so an 'ask' rule on Edit(**)/Write(**) would force a prompt in EVERY mode
and defeat acceptEdits/auto. Leaving edits unlisted makes them mode-driven:
blocked in plan mode, prompted in default mode, auto-accepted in
acceptEdits/auto mode. The deny block below is the hard floor for edits —
it is enforced first and even under bypassPermissions, so secrets/keys/.env
